topic: Split goal-079e2f37 into separate goals. goal-528ecd19 = local harness (Aider+oMLX) operationalization and zero-risk distribution/upgrade paths plus P2 ledger/benchmark explorations (8 stories: #3085 #3100 #2882 #4959 #4954 #2965 #2994 #5410), roadmap arc v0.40.2. Is this a coherent standalone goal or should it split further? One paragraph, then approve / approve with changes / reject.

inputs.claude:
[model=sonnet; version=2.1.327 (Claude Code)]

**Analysis.** goal-528ecd19 is mostly coherent but carries one weak seam. The core is the local harness: Aider+oMLX operationalization (#3085, #3100, #2882) and zero-risk distribution and upgrade paths (#4959, #4954). These share one outcome: a user can install, run and upgrade the local harness without breaking their setup. That outcome is testable, and it matches the Harness Instructions' note that the local harness is a future extension not yet wired up. It maps cleanly to roadmap arc v0.40.2. The distribution and upgrade stories are arguably a separate concern from operationalization, but they depend on it and ship in the same arc, so splitting them would add overhead without adding independent value.

The weak seam is the "P2 ledger/benchmark explorations" group (likely #2965, #2994, #5410). I'm inferring that grouping from the story IDs, because I haven't inspected the stories. Explorations are research spikes. They differ in kind from delivery stories: their outputs are findings, not shippable features, and their completion criteria are looser. They also sit under a P2 priority, while the harness work is the arc's critical path. If they stay in the goal, an exploration that drags on can hold the goal open, and so can hold the v0.40.2 release package open. That is the same failure that made goal-079e2f37 unmanageable at 343 stories, and the reason it is being split in the first place.

The ledger items may also relate to the Tokq bridge and ledger boundary decisions already in memory. That would make them a better fit for a different arc than a local-harness goal.

**Recommendation.** Keep the five harness stories as goal-528ecd19. Move the P2 explorations into a separate "ledger/benchmark exploration" goal, or park them on a later arc with an explicit non-blocking flag. At 8 stories the goal is small enough that I wouldn't split further inside the harness core. The distribution and upgrade stories can stay as an internal ordering, using the umbrella and dependency CLI from #5535 if sequencing matters.

Before finalizing, verify the story-to-theme mapping with `synlynk story show` on each ID. I haven't done that here.

**Position: approve with changes.** Approve goal-528ecd19 as the local harness plus distribution and upgrade goal, and split the P2 ledger/benchmark explorations into their own goal or a deferred arc, so they can't block the v0.40.2 release.

synthesis:
The panel returned one input (claude, sonnet), and it recommends approving with changes. The local-harness core is coherent and shippable as one outcome. A user can install, run and upgrade the Aider+oMLX harness without breaking their setup. That covers operationalization (#3085, #3100, #2882) and zero-risk distribution and upgrade paths (#4959, #4954), and it fits roadmap arc v0.40.2. Splitting distribution and upgrade away from operationalization would add overhead without independent value, since they depend on each other and ship in the same arc. The P2 ledger/benchmark explorations (#2965, #2994, #5410) are the weak seam. They are research spikes whose outputs are findings, not shippable features, and their completion criteria are looser. If they stay in the goal, a slow exploration could hold the goal open and block the v0.40.2 release package. That is the failure mode that made goal-079e2f37 unmanageable at 343 stories. The ledger items may also belong with the Tokq bridge and ledger-boundary work. The panelist inferred which stories are explorations from their IDs and did not inspect them.

Decision: Approve with changes. Goal-528ecd19 becomes the local harness goal (Aider+oMLX operationalization plus zero-risk distribution and upgrade) with five stories (#3085, #3100, #2882, #4959, #4954) on roadmap arc v0.40.2. Move #2965, #2994 and #5410 into a separate ledger/benchmark exploration goal, flagged non-blocking and placed on a later arc or left unscheduled, so they can't hold up the v0.40.2 release. Don't split the harness core further. If ordering between distribution/upgrade and operationalization matters, express it with the umbrella and dependency CLI from #5535. Before applying the split, run `synlynk story show` on all eight IDs to confirm each story's theme matches this grouping. Any story that doesn't match moves to whichever goal fits.
